physics-killer-07.topic: Newton's laws of motion and special relativity
physics-killer-07.goal: Analyze the underlying scientific principles and deduce the correct conclusion.
physics-killer-07.material: As dem observe from Earth, di distance to one star na $6$ light-years. Spaceship leave Earth towards dis star with constant speed $0.6c$ and arrive di star. Which one correctly match, in order, di flight time wey observer for Earth measure and di flight time wey clock inside di spaceship measure? (Take di speed of light $c$ as $1$ light-year/year.)
physics-killer-07.thinking.0: Newton's laws of motion and special relativity
physics-killer-07.s.s1.prompt: As dem observe from Earth, di distance to one star na $6$ light-years. Spaceship leave Earth towards dis star with constant speed $0.6c$ and arrive di star. Which one correctly match, in order, di flight time wey observer for Earth measure and di flight time wey clock inside di spaceship measure? (Take di speed of light $c$ as $1$ light-year/year.)
physics-killer-07.s.s1.explain: Observer for Earth: $\Delta t=\dfrac{6\text{ light-year}}{0.6c}=10$ years. $\gamma=1/\sqrt{1-0.6^2}=1/0.8=1.25$. Di spaceship clock measure both departure and arrival for di same place so na proper time and e be $\Delta t_0=\Delta t/\gamma=10/1.25=8$ years. If you multiply e be $12.5$ years (wrong answer ③), if you divide by $\gamma^2$ e be $6.4$ years (wrong answer ①), and if you swap di two values na wrong answer ④. (From di spaceship point of view, di distance contract to $6/1.25=4.8$ light-years so e match $4.8/0.6=8$ years.)
